name: How much contingency should I leave for hidden problems?

mainEntity.name: How much extra money should I set aside for unexpected issues during a kitchen remodel?
mainEntity.text: How much extra money should I set aside for unexpected issues during a kitchen remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: A contingency fund is essential because kitchen remodels often reveal issues that cannot be fully seen beforehand. In many projects, 10% to 15% of the total budget is a reasonable starting point, but older homes or complex remodels may need more. Common surprises include water damage, termite damage, uneven subfloors, outdated electrical, undersized plumbing, or framing repairs. Without contingency money, homeowners may be forced to downgrade finishes or pause the project when problems appear. The best way to manage this risk is to discuss likely hidden conditions early, especially in older Los Angeles homes. A contractor should be able to explain what kinds of surprises are most common in the specific property type and how they would be priced if discovered.
